claims.text: The base composition is equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The base alloy is a single-phase, disordered solid solution.
The base alloy has a homogeneous chemical distribution.
The base alloy has relatively low hardness and strength.
Deformation of the base alloy is dominated by facile dislocation glide with minimal dislocation accumulation.
The base alloy has a uniform, high stacking-fault energy or a low dislocation-nucleation barrier.
High stacking-fault energy or a low nucleation barrier causes limited dislocation pile-up and weak forest hardening.
Minimal impediment to dislocation glide produces limited work hardening in the base alloy.
A slight Ti-content variation or minor addition can disrupt chemical uniformity while retaining the single-phase state.
A controlled compositional perturbation introduces local obstacles to dislocation motion.
The introduced obstacles promote dislocation pile-ups, tangling, or other dislocation interactions.
Enhanced dislocation accumulation and interaction increase strain hardening.
The modified alloy will exhibit more dislocation pile-ups or tangles than the base alloy during in situ TEM observation.
The compositional perturbation may cause the onset of deformation twinning.
The modified alloy will have higher yield strength than the base alloy.
The modified alloy will have higher hardness than the base alloy.
The proposed mechanism applies only while the alloy remains a single-phase disordered solid solution and avoids deformation-induced phase transformation.

contradictions.description: The intervention proposes inducing nano-precipitation while simultaneously requiring that no secondary phases form and that the alloy remain single phase. Nano-precipitates ordinarily constitute a distinct precipitate phase, so these requirements are internally inconsistent unless the intended heterogeneity is clarified as non-phase-separated clustering.
